inputs.name: case_folded_key
inputs.description: A JSON key in the request body or in a bidder response matches a field of the Go type only when case is ignored (`ID` for `id`).

inputs.name: deep_nesting
inputs.description: A JSON document in the request body or in a bidder response nests 128 levels or more, its outermost value included.

inputs.name: duplicate_keys
inputs.description: A JSON object in the request body or in a bidder response has the same key twice.

inputs.name: invalid_utf8
inputs.description: A JSON string in the request body or in a bidder response holds bytes that are not UTF-8.

inputs.name: options_request
inputs.description: The request's method is OPTIONS: a CORS preflight, or any other OPTIONS, which tower-http's CorsLayer answers as one.

differences.title: Base64url consent strings: Go skips line breaks and ignores unused bits, the base64 crate refuses both
differences.go: `encoding/base64`'s `RawURLEncoding`, which go-gdpr's `ParseString`, the flipp adapter and go-gpp's `NewBitStreamFromBase64` decode consent strings with, skips `\r` and `\n` anywhere in the input, accepts a last digit whose unused bits are set (`QR` is `A`), refuses `=` (the encoding has no padding) and reports `illegal base64 data at input byte N` at the first byte that is neither a digit nor a line break, or at the last byte when the digits end in a lone one.
differences.rust: The base64 crate's `URL_SAFE_NO_PAD` refuses a line break and a last digit with unused bits set, and reports some refusals at another offset or none: it reads the last quantum first (`w=+/+` at 4, where Go says 1) and refuses `AA==` with `Invalid padding` (Go: 2).
differences.visible_in: Which TCF and GPP consent strings decode, and the offset in the warnings Prebid writes from the error: the AMP consent warning (amp/parse.go:143-152) and `GPP consent string is invalid and will be ignored.` (endpoints/openrtb2/auction.go:869-874)
differences.restore: Glue around the base64 crate, pbs-tcf2's `base64` and pbs-gpp's `util::base64`: the line breaks are removed before the crate reads the input, its engine allows unused bits, and a refusal is reported at Go's offset. Rule B (a), since real traffic sends such strings and their consent depends on what decodes, and (d), since Prebid writes the offset into its warnings.

restorations.note: every string of up to 7 symbols over a digit with its low bits zero, one with them set, `\n`, `\r`, `=`, `.` and the two-byte `é` (960,800 strings) decodes through `BitStream::from_base64` to go-gpp's bytes or fails with its text, length by length, against testdata/golden/base64_exhaustive.txt
50,000 seeded strings decode through `BitStream::from_base64` to go-gpp's bytes or fail with its text, batch by batch, against testdata/golden/base64_seeded.txt

every string of up to 7 bytes over a digit with its low bits zero, one with them set, `\n`, `\r`, `=`, `+` and a byte past ASCII (960,800 strings) decodes to go-gdpr's bytes or fails with its text, length by length, against testdata/base64_exhaustive_goldens.json
50,000 seeded strings decode to go-gdpr's bytes or fail with its text, batch by batch, against testdata/base64_seeded_goldens.json

differences.note: The bytes are the crate's. go-gpp pads an incomplete last quantum with `A` before decoding (util/bitstream.go:35-41), which is go-gpp's own logic and is ported as it is.

differences.title: Parity bodies and meta headers: Go's `base64.StdEncoding` skips line breaks and ignores unused bits, the base64 crate refuses both
differences.go: A body's `b64` member and the `X-Parity-Meta` header are decoded with `base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString` (parity/body.go:67, parity/transport/meta.go:28): it skips `\r` and `\n` anywhere, accepts a last digit whose unused bits are set (`aGl=` is `hi`), and reports `illegal base64 data at input byte N`.
differences.rust: The base64 crate's `STANDARD` engine refuses a line break and a last digit with unused bits set, and words its errors its own way: `body.b64: Invalid symbol 33, offset 0.` where Go says `body.b64: illegal base64 data at input byte 0`.
differences.visible_in: Which `b64` bodies and `X-Parity-Meta` values the Rust server reads, and the error texts, for values the runner never writes: it encodes them with `base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString`
differences.restore: Glue that drops line breaks and clears unused bits before decoding, as pbs-tcf2's `base64` does for consent strings; not planned, since only the runner writes these values.

differences.title: Large stored-data entries: freecache refuses them, moka keeps them
differences.go: freecache refuses an entry whose key and value together are longer than 1/1024 of the cache less its 24-byte entry header (`ErrLargeEntry`, whose text says only 1/1024; freecache's segment.go:73-76): a 1 MiB cache keeps a 993-byte document under a 7-byte key, 1000 bytes in all, and refuses a 994-byte one. Prebid logs the error and drops the entry (stored_requests/caches/memory/maps.go:60-64), so such a document is fetched again on every request.
differences.rust: moka, bounded by the same byte budget through a weigher, keeps every entry that fits the budget.
differences.visible_in: Fetches and error logs of the stored request, imp, response and account caches when a document is larger than 1/1024 of its in-memory cache

differences.title: Boolean `PBS_` variables: Viper converts them with `cast.ToBool`, the config crate with its own spellings
differences.go: For a key with a bool default, Viper converts a `PBS_` value with `cast.ToBool` (`SetTypeByDefaultValue`, config/config.go:1319), which is `strconv.ParseBool` with its error dropped: `1`, `t`, `T`, `true`, `TRUE` and `True` are true, and every other value (`tRuE`, `yes`, `YES`, `on`, `y`, `maybe` and the false forms) is false, never an error. A key bound only with `BindEnv` goes through mapstructure's weak decode: `ParseBool`, the empty string is false, and anything else fails the load (orchestrator ruling 8).
differences.rust: The config crate takes `1`, `true`, `on` and `yes` and their false forms (`0`, `false`, `off`, `no`) in any case, and fails the load on `t`, `T`, `f`, `F`, `y`, `n` and `maybe`.
differences.visible_in: Startup with `PBS_` environment variables that set boolean keys
differences.restore: CONFIG-LOADER converts as Viper does: `cast.ToBool` for keys with a bool default, and mapstructure's weak decode for keys bound only with `BindEnv` (`adapters.<bidder>.disabled`, `.debug.allow`, `.experiment.adsCert.enabled`, `.modifyingVastXmlAllowed`, `account_defaults.privacy.dsa.gdpr_only` and the others the defaults table marks), each path against a Go golden of its own (orchestrator ruling 8).

differences.title: Booleans in pbs.yaml: Viper converts yaml.v3's untyped value with `cast.ToBool`, the config crate takes serde-saphyr's
differences.go: Viper takes a pbs.yaml value as yaml.v3 resolves it untyped (`true`, `True`, `TRUE` and their false forms are booleans, `yes`, `on`, `y` and `tRuE` stay strings, `1` is a number) and converts it with `cast.ToBool` for a key with a bool default, so `true`, `True`, `t` and `1` are true, and `yes`, `on`, `y`, `tRuE`, `maybe` and every false form are false, never an error.
differences.rust: Through serde-saphyr and the config crate, `yes`, `on`, `y` and `tRuE` are true, `n`, `no` and `off` are false, and `t`, `f` and `maybe` fail the load.
differences.visible_in: Startup with a pbs.yaml that sets a boolean key
differences.restore: CONFIG-LOADER converts pbs.yaml values as Viper does: `cast.ToBool` after yaml.v3's untyped resolution (orchestrator ruling 8).

differences.title: Config keys: Viper lower-cases them, the config crate keeps file keys as written
differences.go: Viper lower-cases every key, so `Port:`, `port:` and `PORT:` in pbs.yaml all set `port`.
differences.rust: The config crate keeps file keys as written: only `port:` sets `port`, and the other spellings are ignored, so the default stays.
differences.visible_in: Startup with a pbs.yaml whose keys are not in lower case
differences.restore: CONFIG-LOADER lower-cases file and environment keys, as Viper does.

differences.title: Set-Cookie attribute order: `http.Cookie` and the cookie crate write the same attributes in different orders
differences.go: `http.Cookie.String` writes `uids=eyJ1aWRzIjp7fX0=; Path=/; Domain=pbs.example; Expires=Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:20:30 GMT; Secure; SameSite=None` (usersync/cookie.go:93-113).
differences.rust: The cookie crate writes the same attributes and value, the base64 padding raw, in another order: `uids=eyJ1aWRzIjp7fX0=; SameSite=None; Secure; Path=/; Domain=pbs.example; Expires=Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:20:30 GMT`.
differences.visible_in: The Set-Cookie header that writes the uids cookie (/setuid and /optout)
differences.note: The cookie's value, the uids JSON in base64, keeps Go's format under Rule B (b), and the harness compares it as JSON after base64 decoding.

differences.title: Global vendor lists: Go reads them with `encoding/json`, the port with serde
differences.go: go-gdpr's `vendorlist2.ParseEagerly` reads a fetched list with `json.Unmarshal` into its contract: member names match ignoring case (`ſ` and the Kelvin sign as `s` and `k`), a repeated member is read again (a second `vendors` adds its vendors), a string where a list of ids belongs is decoded as standard base64 (`"purposes":"AQID"` is 1, 2 and 3), a key that is not UTF-8 or holds a lone surrogate escape reads with U+FFFD, a skipped member nested past 10000 levels and an array where an object of the contract belongs are refused, and the errors are `encoding/json`'s (`invalid character 'm' looking for beginning of value`).
differences.rust: serde_json reads it into the same contract, so the json.* entries apply: member names match exactly (`json.key-case`), and a repeated member (`json.duplicate-keys`), a key that is not UTF-8 (`json.invalid-utf8`) or holds a lone surrogate (`json.lone-surrogates`) and a string where a list of ids belongs are refused; a skipped member is read at any depth (`json.nesting-depth`); an array of a contract's members, in their order, is read as the contract; and the errors are serde_json's (`expected value at line 1 column 1`). A `null` leaves Go's zero value, and IAB's lists are well-formed: every GVL fixture of go-gdpr and prebid-server reads as in Go.
differences.visible_in: Whether a fetched vendor list is kept for GDPR enforcement, and the error of the `GET ... returned malformed JSON` log line (gdpr/vendorlist-fetching.go:150-154)
differences.restore: A Go-compatible JSON reader for the vendor list; not planned (orchestrator ruling 2), since IAB publishes well-formed lists.
differences.note: `crates/tcf2/tests/vendorlist.rs::gvl_corpus` counts, per reason, how the 5,017 documents of the two Go corpora read beside Go. Reading the list through JSONUTIL's decode entry for outside bytes, once it merges (orchestrator ruling 7), would restore keys with a lone surrogate.

differences.title: Parity bodies: flate2 writes and reads their gzip, and a `Content-Encoding` holding U+0130 is not gzip
differences.go: A body's content is compressed with `gzip.NewWriter` and inflated with `gzip.NewReader` (parity/body.go:111-148), under the trimmed `Content-Encoding` lower-cased by `strings.ToLower`, which maps U+0130 to `i`, so `GZ\u0130P` is gzip (parity/body.go:104); an empty gzip body fails with `gzip decode: EOF`.
differences.rust: flate2 compresses the same content to other bytes (`gzip.payload-bytes`) and words its errors its own way (`gzip decode: unexpected end of file` for an empty body), and `str::to_lowercase` maps U+0130 to `i` and U+0307, so under `GZ\u0130P` a recorded body is kept as `b64` without `json` and an input body is refused (`unsupported content encoding`).
differences.visible_in: The trace's recorded bodies and the bodies the Rust server sends for an envelope: their gzip bytes, and the reading of a `Content-Encoding` the runner never writes
differences.restore: Go's case mapping of U+0130 for the encoding name; not planned, since no content coding is spelled with it (RFC 9110 codings are ASCII tokens).

differences.title: Gzip bytes: compress/gzip and flate2 write different deflate streams of the same payload
differences.go: `compress/gzip` at the default level writes Go's deflate stream, and its `Close` adds an empty stored block: 129 bytes for the pinned bid request (exchange/bidder.go:848-880).
differences.rust: flate2 (miniz_oxide) writes another valid stream, 128 bytes for the same request, with the same 10-byte header (`1f 8b 08 00`, MTIME 0, XFL 0, OS 255). Both inflate to the same bytes; a bidder sees other compressed bytes and another Content-Length.
differences.visible_in: The bodies and Content-Length of bidder requests sent with `endpoint_compression: gzip`

differences.title: Caller-set Accept-Encoding or Range: Go's Transport leaves the response compressed, reqwest decompresses it
differences.go: The Transport asks for gzip and decompresses only when the request has neither `Accept-Encoding` nor `Range`; an adapter that sets `Accept-Encoding` itself (gamma.go:136) or sends a `Range` gets the compressed body with `Content-Encoding` and `Content-Length` (net/http/transport.go `persistConn.roundTrip`).
differences.rust: reqwest's gzip asks for gzip unless the caller set `Accept-Encoding`, even beside a `Range`, and decompresses every gzip response, so such an adapter gets the decompressed body without `Content-Encoding` or `Content-Length`.
differences.visible_in: Bids of adapters that set Accept-Encoding or Range, when the bidder answers with gzip
differences.restore: A second client with gzip off for requests whose adapter set Accept-Encoding (not planned).

differences.title: Connection metrics: httptrace hooks in Go, reconstructed events here
differences.go: bidder.go's httptrace hooks (exchange/bidder.go:732-798) take `GetConn` to `GotConn` as the connection wait with its `Reused` flag, which also moves a bidder's `http_client.throttle` health when the connection was reused, `DNSStart` to `DNSDone` as the DNS time, `TLSHandshakeStart` to `TLSHandshakeDone` as the TLS handshake time and, when `metrics.disabled_metrics.adapter_connections_dial_metrics` is false, `ConnectStart` to `ConnectDone` as the adapter's dial time, a dial that fails counting as a dial error.
differences.rust: The clients report `Event::Dns` from their resolver and `Event::GotConn` off the response, its reuse read from the connection's addresses and its wait the wait for the `max_connections_per_host` slot alone, so a new connection's wait leaves out its dial and a request that fails before its response head reports no `GotConn`; there is no dial or TLS handshake event, so no TLS handshake time, dial time or dial error is recorded.
differences.visible_in: The adapter connection created, reused, wait, dial time and dial error metrics, the DNS and TLS handshake time metrics, and bidder throttling under `http_client.throttle`
differences.restore: A connector layer that times dials and TLS handshakes, once tower-layer and tower-service are in the crate stack.

differences.title: Default Accept: reqwest sends `Accept: */*`, net/http sends none
differences.go: `net/http` adds no `Accept`, so the currency and vendor-list GETs and the adapter requests that set none carry no `Accept` (currency/rate_converter.go:53).
differences.rust: reqwest 0.13.5's `ClientBuilder::new` puts `Accept: */*` among the client's default headers, so every request without an `Accept` of its own carries it; a caller's `Accept` replaces it.
differences.visible_in: Outbound requests whose caller set no Accept
differences.restore: None in reqwest's API: `ClientBuilder::default_headers` only adds to the defaults and cannot drop one. Accepted under Rule A (orchestrator ruling 9); HTTP-CLIENT may add a crate-level pin.

differences.title: Currency and analytics client: Go's DefaultTransport negotiates HTTP/2, the plain client stays on HTTP/1.1
differences.go: `http.DefaultTransport`, which the currency fetch (main.go:72) and the analytics client (analytics/clients/http.go) use, offers h2 over TLS and, to a server that takes it, sends HTTP/2 with `User-Agent: Go-http-client/2.0`.
differences.rust: The plain client speaks HTTP/1.1 to every server and sends `User-Agent: Go-http-client/1.1`; HTTP-H2 gives h2 to the bidder client only.
differences.visible_in: Requests of the currency fetch and the analytics modules to servers that offer h2

differences.title: A POST, PUT or PATCH without a body: Go sends `Content-Length: 0`, hyper sends no length
differences.go: `Request.write` writes `Content-Length: 0` for a POST, PUT or PATCH whose body is empty (`transferWriter.shouldSendContentLength`), as bidder.go's `bytes.NewBuffer(req.Body)` of an empty body is, and no length for another method without a body.
differences.rust: hyper writes no `Content-Length` for a request whose body is empty, whatever its method; the clients drop a caller's `Content-Length` entry, as Go does.
differences.visible_in: Requests without a body sent with POST, PUT or PATCH, which a server that requires a length refuses (`411 Length Required`)
differences.restore: Set `Content-Length: 0` in the clients' pass over the caller's headers for those methods when the body is empty, which hyper then writes (not planned: no Rule B case).

differences.title: Error texts: Go's `*url.Error` texts, reqwest's error chains
differences.go: A request that fails reads `Post "http://127.0.0.1:PORT/e": EOF` when the server closes the connection, `Post "http://127.0.0.1:PORT/e": dial tcp 127.0.0.1:PORT: connect: connection refused` when nothing listens, and `Get "https://bidder.test/p?q=1": Forbidden` when a proxy refuses the CONNECT, in bidder errors and debug output. The URL is the request's as `URL.String` writes it back, `http://127.0.0.1:PORT?x=1` for one without a path, or the hop that failed after a redirect (net/http/client.go `Client.do`).
differences.rust: The same `<Method> "<url>"` shape, then reqwest's chain: `error sending request: client error (SendRequest): connection closed before message completed`, `error sending request: client error (Connect): tcp connect error: Connection refused (os error 111)` on Linux, and `error sending request: client error (Connect): tunnel error: unsuccessful`. The URL is the url crate's serialisation, which writes a URL without a path with `/` (`http://127.0.0.1:PORT/?x=1`), and a hop that fails after a redirect goes by the first request's URL, the only one reqwest's error keeps. A deadline stays `context deadline exceeded`, which bidder.go:616-620 reports.
differences.visible_in: Bidder error messages in the response's `ext` with debug on, and the logs

differences.title: Gzip responses at the edges: upper case, empty bodies and corrupt streams
differences.go: The Transport decompresses a `Content-Encoding` of `gzip` in any case (`GZIP`), keeps `Content-Encoding` and `Content-Length` on a gzip response without a body (a 204, or `Content-Length: 0`), and reads a gzip body too short for its header as `unexpected EOF`.
differences.rust: reqwest decompresses a lower-case `gzip` only, so a `GZIP` body reaches the adapter compressed; it drops `Content-Encoding` and `Content-Length` of the empty responses; and a corrupt body reads as `error decoding response body: Invalid gzip header`.
differences.visible_in: Bidder responses with an upper-case gzip Content-Encoding, an empty gzip body or a corrupt one

differences.title: Header names: Go writes them canonicalised, hyper in lower case
differences.go: `Header.Set` canonicalises names (`Content-Type`), and `Request.write` writes each name as the map holds it.
differences.rust: hyper writes every name as the `HeaderMap` holds it, in lower case, on HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2.
differences.visible_in: The header names of every outbound request
differences.restore: reqwest's `http1_title_case_headers`, one builder line (not planned).

differences.title: Header order: Go sorts the headers, hyper keeps the order they were set in
differences.go: `Request.write` writes `Host`, `User-Agent` and `Content-Length` first, then the other headers sorted by name, then the Transport's `Accept-Encoding`.
differences.rust: hyper writes the caller's headers in the order they were set, then `User-Agent`, `Accept` and `Accept-Encoding`, then `Host` and `Content-Length`.
differences.visible_in: The header order of every outbound request

differences.title: Header values: Go trims the white space around each one, hyper writes them as set
differences.go: `Request.write` writes every header value without the spaces and tabs around it (`Header.writeSubset`, `textproto.TrimString`), so a value of `  padded value  ` goes out as `padded value` and one of spaces as an empty value.
differences.rust: hyper writes each value as the `HeaderMap` holds it, spaces and tabs included; the clients trim `User-Agent` alone (http-client.user-agent).
differences.visible_in: The header values of bidder requests whose adapter copies a publisher value with white space around it (a page URL, a user agent, an IP) into a header other than User-Agent
differences.restore: Trim every value in the clients' pass over the caller's headers, as `User-Agent`'s is (not planned: no Rule B case).

differences.title: Host line: Go writes the URL's host as written, hyper the url crate's normal form
differences.go: `Request.write` writes the URL's host as written, port included (`Bidder.Example.COM:80`), and never a `Host` entry of the header map; bidder-info endpoints such as logan's `http://USeast2.logan.ai/pserver` have upper-case letters in their host.
differences.rust: The url crate lower-cases the host and drops the scheme's default port (url.host-normalization), so hyper writes `bidder.example.com`.
differences.visible_in: The Host header of requests to endpoints whose host has upper-case letters or names its scheme's port

differences.title: max_connections_per_host: Go's Transport waits at the limit, reqwest has no limit
differences.go: `MaxConnsPerHost` lets a host have that many connections, and a request that needs one more waits until one is free.
differences.rust: reqwest has no per-host connection limit.
differences.visible_in: Bidder request latency and connection counts under `max_connections_per_host`
differences.restore: pbs-http-client keeps a semaphore per connect key (proxy, scheme and address, as Go keys its connections) whose slot a request holds from its send until its body is read: with a limit of 1, three concurrent requests run one after the other on one connection, as Go's do. The slots count requests in flight where Go counts connections, which over HTTP/1.1 carry one request at a time.

differences.title: max_idle_connections: Go caps idle connections across hosts, reqwest per host only
differences.go: `MaxIdleConns` caps the idle connections of all hosts together and closes the oldest when another goes idle past the cap.
differences.rust: reqwest caps idle connections per host only, so with `max_idle_connections: 1` a client keeps an idle connection to each host and reuses it.
differences.visible_in: Open connections and new dials of clients that reach many hosts

differences.title: Proxy environment: Go's ProxyFromEnvironment rules, reqwest's own
differences.go: `http.ProxyFromEnvironment` (golang.org/x/net/http/httpproxy) reads `HTTP_PROXY` and `HTTPS_PROXY`, the upper-case names first, excepts the hosts, domains, IPs and CIDRs of `NO_PROXY`, never proxies `localhost` or a loopback address, does not read `ALL_PROXY`, and refuses `HTTP_PROXY` under `REQUEST_METHOD`.
differences.rust: reqwest's system proxies read `ALL_PROXY` too, match `NO_PROXY` by their own rules and proxy loopback addresses that `NO_PROXY` does not name.
differences.visible_in: Where outbound requests go when the operator sets proxy variables
differences.restore: pbs-http-client reads the variables once into a `ProxyEnv` and picks each request's proxy with a port of httpproxy's rules behind `Proxy::custom`; over 39 environments and 101 URLs it picks Go's proxy, but for http-client.proxy-exceptions. Loopback is never proxied, which also keeps parity traffic on the machine.

restorations.note: requests_reach_the_proxy_like_go shows what a proxy receives: the absolute-form request and the CONNECT with Go's `User-Agent`.

differences.title: Proxy picks that still differ: `LocalHost`, IPv6 zones and proxy values without a URL's host
differences.go: httpproxy compares the host with `localhost` before it lower-cases it, so it proxies `http://LocalHost/`; `url.Parse` reads an IPv6 zone in a request's URL (`http://[fe80::1%25en0]/`) or a proxy's; a proxy value such as `bogus url` is used as the URL `bogus%20url`, whose dial fails; and the Transport dials a proxy whose host `url.Parse` reads as empty on the local machine (net/http/transport.go `canonicalAddr`): `:3128`, read as `http://:3128`, at port 3128, and `//proxy.test:8080`, `/proxy` or `http:proxy.test` at port 80.
differences.rust: The url crate lower-cases the host, and the clients never proxy localhost in any case; it parses no IPv6 zone, so such a URL makes no request and such a proxy is refused; the clients refuse a proxy value the url crate reads as no http or https URL with a host (`bogus url`, `http://:3128`); and the url crate takes the host of `http:////proxy.test:8080`, `http:///proxy` and `http:proxy.test` from what follows the scheme, so the clients dial `proxy.test:8080`, `proxy:80` and `proxy.test:80`.
differences.visible_in: Requests to `LocalHost` or a zoned IPv6 address under a proxy environment, and proxy variables that hold no URL, a zoned IPv6 proxy or a URL whose host Go reads as empty

differences.title: Redirects: Go's default CheckRedirect and reqwest's policy differ on methods, headers and the error
differences.go: At most 10 redirects; 301 and 302 turn every method but GET and HEAD into a GET without a body, as 303 does, and 307 and 308 resend both; the content headers go with the body; `Authorization` and `Cookie` reach the first request's host and its subdomains on any port; a caller's `Referer` is kept; and the 11th redirect fails with `Get "/r/10": stopped after 10 redirects`, the Location as the server wrote it (net/http/client.go).
differences.rust: The same limit and 303, 307 and 308 rules, but a PUT keeps its method and body on a 301 or 302, a GET keeps its content headers, the sensitive headers are dropped on any change of host, port or scheme from the previous hop (a subdomain or another port included), the previous URL replaces the caller's `Referer`, and the error names the absolute URL.
differences.visible_in: Bidder requests whose endpoint answers with a redirect

differences.title: Request-target: Go writes `url.Parse` then `RequestURI`, reqwest the url crate's WHATWG serialisation
differences.go: Go sends the path re-escaped only where it is no valid encoding (`|`, `^` and a backslash escaped, dot segments kept) and the query as written, so a space, quote, apostrophe, `<`, `>` or non-ASCII byte in it goes out raw; it refuses a URL with a control character or a malformed escape in the path.
differences.rust: The url crate escapes those query bytes, resolves dot segments, reads a backslash as a slash, keeps `|` and `^`, drops tabs and newlines and keeps a malformed escape. Over the 409 adapter fixture URIs and the 393 rendered bidder-info endpoints every target is Go's.
differences.visible_in: The request line of bidder requests whose URL holds such bytes, which adapters that write publisher values into their URL unescaped can send
differences.restore: Build the request's Url from Go's escaped target (not planned: the 2026-11-19 ruling accepts the crate).

differences.title: SOCKS proxies: Go's Transport dials them, the clients refuse them
differences.go: A `socks5://` or `socks5h://` value of `HTTP_PROXY` or `HTTPS_PROXY` sends requests through that SOCKS5 proxy (net/http/transport.go `Transport.dialConn`).
differences.rust: The clients refuse such a request with `HTTP_PROXY names a "socks5" proxy, and only http and https proxies are supported`, the value left out as it may hold credentials; reqwest's socks feature is not in the crate stack.
differences.visible_in: Every outbound request when the proxy variables name a SOCKS proxy
differences.restore: reqwest's socks feature (tokio-socks) through STACK, with the proxy rules handing it the socks URLs (not planned).

differences.title: Deadline errors: Go's are `context.DeadlineExceeded`, reqwest's are its own
differences.go: A request that runs past its context deadline fails with `context deadline exceeded` (ctxhttp returns `ctx.Err()`), which bidder.go reports as `errortypes.Timeout` and counts in the timeout metrics (exchange/bidder.go:616-620). A caller that calls `client.Do` itself gets `Post "<url>": context deadline exceeded`, and a client with a `Timeout` that ends first adds ` (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)`, or ` (Client.Timeout or context cancellation while reading body)` to a body error (net/http/client.go).
differences.rust: reqwest's own timeout fails with `operation timed out` inside its error chain, and the caller tells it apart with `reqwest::Error::is_timeout`.
differences.visible_in: Bidder timeout errors in responses, and the timeout metrics
differences.restore: pbs-http-client sends each request and reads its body under the deadline, and ends one past it with `ErrorKind::DeadlineExceeded`, which reads `context deadline exceeded` and whose `is_timeout` is bidder.go's test; Prebid's error codes and timeout metrics follow it for a send error, and a body error stays unclassified, as bidder.go returns it. `RequestError::do_text` keeps `client.Do`'s text for the callers that call it (the floors fetcher, the currency fetch, scope3), and `Client::with_timeout` is Go's `Client.Timeout`, failing with `ErrorKind::ClientTimeout` and Go's texts.

differences.title: TLS handshake timeout: Go's Transport has one, reqwest has none
differences.go: `TLSHandshakeTimeout` (`tls_handshake_timeout_seconds`, 10 s by default for each of router.go's clients, router/router.go:155) ends a stalled handshake with `Get "https://...": net/http: TLS handshake timeout`, which bidder.go does not count as a timeout.
differences.rust: reqwest has no handshake timeout: `dialer.timeout_seconds` (30 s by default), which reqwest applies to the dial and the handshake together, and the request's deadline bound it, so under a deadline longer than the handshake timeout a stalled handshake ends as `context deadline exceeded`, a timeout. A shorter deadline ends it so in both.
differences.visible_in: Requests to a server that stalls the TLS handshake under a deadline longer than the handshake timeout: their errors and the timeout metrics
differences.note: `expect_continue_timeout_seconds` has no counterpart either: only a request with `Expect: 100-continue` waits for a `100 Continue`, and Prebid sends none.

differences.title: Redirects through a caller's transport: Go's Client follows them hop by hop, the client leaves them to the transport
differences.go: `Client.do` follows a redirect whatever the RoundTripper, calling it again for each hop, so a RoundTripper under the client, as the parity transport is, sees every hop as a call of its own, and an answer it makes with a `Location` is followed (net/http/client.go:597-755).
differences.rust: `Client::send` returns the transport's answer as it is. A Builder's transport follows redirects inside reqwest, so a transport wrapped around it sees the chain as one call, and the redirect answer of a transport that does not go to the network comes back unfollowed.
differences.visible_in: The parity harness's outbound calls for a bidder that redirects, and a mocked answer with a redirect; router.go's clients follow redirects as `http-client.redirects` says
differences.restore: `Client::send` follows each redirect, calling its transport again for the next hop under Go's `CheckRedirect` rules, and a Builder's transport follows none itself: the redirect rules move from reqwest's policy into the client.

differences.title: Unreachable bidders: Go's errors hold `ECONNREFUSED` and `*net.DNSError`, reqwest's say only that the connect failed
differences.go: bidder.go reports a failed request as seat non-bid code 103, an unreachable bidder, when `errors.Is(err, syscall.ECONNREFUSED)` holds or `errors.As` finds a `*net.DNSError` whose `IsNotFound` holds, as Go's resolvers set it for a name that does not exist or has no address, and as 100 otherwise (exchange/non_bid_reason.go:41-57, net/cgo_unix.go:189-190).
differences.rust: reqwest's errors say only that the connect failed, and std turns getaddrinfo's code into `gai_strerror`'s text, so neither cause can be read off them: every such request would be 100.
differences.visible_in: `ext.seatnonbid` status codes, 103 against 100, for bidder requests refused at the connect or sent to a host name that does not exist
differences.restore: pbs-http-client keeps each error's causes behind `Error::source`: `RequestError::is_connection_refused` finds the refused dial's I/O error, and the clients' resolver fails with a `DnsError`, not found for the texts glibc and macOS give `EAI_NONAME` and `EAI_NODATA` and musl gives `EAI_NONAME`, an empty answer and a `.invalid` name, which `RequestError::is_dns_not_found` finds; a transport of the caller's makes either cause itself.

differences.title: Default User-Agent: net/http sends `Go-http-client/1.1`, reqwest sends none
differences.go: `net/http` sends `User-Agent: Go-http-client/1.1` when the caller set none.
differences.rust: reqwest sends no `User-Agent` at all.
differences.visible_in: Outbound requests whose caller set no User-Agent: bidder requests without one, and the currency and vendor-list fetches
differences.restore: HTTP-CLIENT sets `Go-http-client/1.1` when the caller set none, one line of client config (D-UA, orchestrator ruling 5), and HTTP-H2 keeps it on HTTP/2.

restorations.note: The general client writes Go's `User-Agent` line for every case of headers.json: `Go-http-client/1.1` when the caller set none, the first of two values, and none for an empty one.

differences.title: A raw control character after an escape in a string, or in a small struct's member name: jsoniter reads it, serde_json rejects the document
differences.go: JSON forbids a raw U+0000 to U+001F inside a string. jsoniter (`jsonutil.Unmarshal`, `UnmarshalValid` and `MergeClone`) rejects one that comes before the first backslash of its string but reads the rest of the string unchecked from that backslash on, so it reads a raw tab or line break that follows an escape such as `\n` or `\"`: in a field, a map key, an unknown member and a `json.RawMessage`, which keeps it as written (iter_str.go:9-52, iter_skip_strict.go:61-83). It matches the member names of a struct of ten fields or fewer by a hash that checks none of their bytes, so a member whose name holds one anywhere passes there, matching no field (reflect_struct_decoder.go:47, iter_object.go:49-96). `encoding/json` rejects them all.
differences.rust: serde_json rejects every raw control character in a string, as `encoding/json` does, so the document fails to decode and `merge_clone` fails.
differences.visible_in: The status of requests, and the handling of bidder responses, that hold such a string (an `adm` of markup that escapes its quotes but keeps raw line breaks or tabs)
differences.restore: Escape each raw control character that follows a backslash in its string before serde_json reads the bytes, as `replace_lone_surrogates` rewrites lone surrogates (a raw member would then hold the escape, as in `json.lone-surrogates-raw`), and drop members whose names hold one where the target has ten fields or fewer; not planned (D-DECODE).

differences.title: Control characters: jsoniter writes `\u0008` and `\u000c`, encoding/json and serde_json `\b` and `\f`
differences.go: jsoniter (`jsonutil.Marshal`) writes U+0008 and U+000C as `\u0008` and `\u000c`; `json.Marshal` and the endpoints' Encoders (Go 1.22 and later) write `\b` and `\f`. The other control characters are `\u00XX` in all of them, and DEL is written as it is.
differences.rust: serde_json writes `\b` and `\f`, as `encoding/json` does; the other control characters are `\u00XX`, and DEL is written as it is.
differences.visible_in: Strings holding U+0008 or U+000C in what `jsonutil.Marshal` wrote: ext members, adapter request bodies and cache payloads
differences.note: Its mismatches are lexical `unicode_escape`, which the pattern of `json.html-escape` takes everywhere, so the harness counts them there: one pattern per class and path.

differences.title: A decode into a value that already holds a slice: jsoniter decodes into the elements there, the port builds new ones
differences.go: `jsonutil.Unmarshal` into a value that already holds a slice decodes each array element into the element at its index while the slice's capacity lasts, so the members an element leaves out keep the old element's. `config.UnpackDSADefault` decodes an account's DSA default into the `DefaultUnpacked` the account defaults left (account/fetcher.go:152, account/account.go:71), so an account's transparency entry keeps the `domain` or `dsaparams` of the host's entry at its index where it leaves them out.
differences.rust: serde builds every value new. `merge_clone`, the port's decode into a value that holds data, keeps what the document leaves out as Go does, but replaces a slice with new elements, as Go's `MergeClone` does.
differences.visible_in: The DSA object (`regs.ext.dsa`) Prebid fills into bid requests from the DSA default of an account whose transparency entries leave out members the host's account defaults set
differences.restore: Merge each array element into the element at its index where `UnpackDSADefault` is ported; not planned (D-DECODE).

differences.title: Duplicate JSON keys: Go keeps the last, the serde derives reject the document
differences.go: jsoniter and `encoding/json` keep the last of duplicate keys.
differences.rust: The serde derives reject the document (`duplicate field`); a `serde_json::Value` keeps the last key, as Go does.
differences.visible_in: The status of requests whose JSON repeats a key, and the handling of such bidder responses
differences.restore: Decode again through `serde_json::Value` on that error, the last key winning; not planned (D-DECODE).

differences.title: Decode and encode errors: Prebid's wrappers are kept, the library message inside them is serde_json's
differences.go: `jsonutil.Unmarshal` and `UnmarshalValid` fail with a `FailedToUnmarshal` holding jsoniter's message trimmed by `tryExtractErrorMessage` (`cannot unmarshal main.idTarget.ID: expects " or n, but found 1`, `there are bytes left after unmarshal`), `Marshal` with a `FailedToMarshal`, and MergeClone with `cannot unmarshal <Type.Field>: <message>`; Prebid puts the text into its own (`Invalid request format: ...`).
differences.rust: The same wrappers, error types and Prebid texts (`invalid type`, `invalid json on existing object`), with serde_json's message inside (`trailing characters` and its position where jsoniter says `there are bytes left after unmarshal`).
differences.visible_in: The texts of 400 responses, of `ext.errors` and `ext.warnings`, and of the bidder errors Prebid reports, wherever a JSON decode or encode failed
differences.restore: Write jsoniter's messages from serde_json's error categories; not planned (D-DECODE).

differences.title: `FindElement` on a malformed value: Go fails with `encoding/json`'s text, the port with serde_json's
differences.go: `FindElement` and `DropElement` fail with `encoding/json`'s message where a value the walk reads is malformed (`invalid character 'x' after object key:value pair` for `1x`) or beyond float64's range (`json: cannot unmarshal number 1e400 into Go value of type float64`), and read a key that is not UTF-8 as U+FFFD and go on.
differences.rust: The walk fails there too, with serde_json's message, and fails on a key that is not UTF-8 (`json.invalid-utf8`).
differences.visible_in: Nothing in production: the one caller, the Audience Network adapter (adapters/audienceNetwork/facebook.go:101), passes the body it has just marshalled, which is valid JSON

differences.title: `FindElement` and `DropElement`: Go cuts at the offsets of `encoding/json`'s token walk, which serde_json has no equivalent of
differences.go: `jsonutil.FindElement` walks the document with `encoding/json`'s `Decoder` (`Token`, `Decode`, `More`, `InputOffset`) and returns the span of the first member named, with one neighbouring comma; its errors are the decoder's (`EOF`, `unexpected EOF`, the state machine's texts) and its comma and colon scans panic past the end. `DropElement` cuts the span out of the bytes, which the Audience Network adapter sends as the request body.
differences.rust: serde_json has no token decoder: reading the document as a `Value` and writing it back loses the input's bytes, Go's offsets and its errors.
differences.visible_in: The Audience Network adapter's request body, `consented_providers_settings` cut out (adapters/audienceNetwork/facebook.go:101)
differences.restore: `find_element` and `drop_element` port the walk's states, errors, offsets and index panics, with serde_json reading each scalar and the matched value: Prebid-authored bytes.

restorations.note: `TestDropElement`'s cases and the decoder's edges: offsets, bytes, error texts and panics.
50,000 seeded documents and paths give Go's offsets, bytes, error texts and panics byte for byte.

differences.title: Float spelling: Go writes `1`, `300` and `1e-07` where serde_json writes `1.0`, `300.0` and `1e-7`
differences.go: strconv's shortest form, plain for `1e-6 <= |f| < 1e21` (1e20 is `100000000000000000000`) and with an exponent otherwise, which jsoniter (`jsonutil.Marshal`) writes `1e-07` and `encoding/json` (`json.Marshal` in 222 adapter files, the endpoints' Encoders) `1e-7`. A float32 is written at 32 bits, an integral value has no fraction (`1`, `300`) and -0 stays `-0`. A number read into `interface{}` is a float64: `12345678901234567890` comes back as `12345678901234567000`, and `300.0` and `1E2` as `300` and `100`.
differences.rust: serde_json writes `1.0`, `300.0`, `123456789.0` and `1e+20`; an f64 0.000001 is `1e-6` and an f32 one `0.000001`, and -0 is `-0.0`. A `serde_json::Value` keeps integers exact and floats as f64: `300.0`, `100.0`, `1e-6`, `-0.0`.
differences.visible_in: Prices and other floats in response bodies, bidder request bodies, analytics and cache payloads
differences.restore: A serde_json Formatter overriding `write_f64` and `write_f32`; not planned (orchestrator ruling 2).
differences.note: Floats Prebid prints into its own text (targeting values, macros) use the precision Prebid's Go code uses, which is Prebid logic ported in place (orchestrator ruling 4), not this entry.

differences.title: HTML escaping: Go writes `<`, `>` and `&` as `\u` escapes, serde_json as they are
differences.go: `jsonutil.Marshal` (jsoniter's `ConfigCompatibleWithStandardLibrary`), `json.Marshal` and Encoders with default settings write `<`, `>` and `&` in strings as `\u003c`, `\u003e` and `\u0026`, and U+2028 and U+2029 as `\u2028` and `\u2029`. Inside a `json.RawMessage` only `json.Marshal` and such Encoders escape: `jsonutil.Marshal` writes one through the `RawMessageExtension` main.go:23-25 registers, which compacts it and escapes nothing (`json.raw-not-compacted`). The endpoints' Encoders turn HTML escaping off (`SetEscapeHTML(false)` at endpoints/openrtb2/auction.go:384, endpoints/openrtb2/amp_auction.go:408, endpoints/cookie_sync.go:561 and exchange/exchange.go:986) and still escape U+2028 and U+2029 in strings.
differences.rust: serde_json writes all five characters as they are. Strings the endpoints' Encoders write themselves, such as a bid's `adm`, differ only in U+2028 and U+2029; the `<`, `>` and `&` differences sit in what `jsonutil.Marshal` and `json.Marshal` wrote: ext members, adapter request bodies and cache payloads.
differences.visible_in: Response bodies, bidder request bodies and Prebid Cache payloads
differences.restore: A serde_json Formatter that adds Go's escapes; not planned (D-HTMLESC).
differences.note: The `unicode_escape` pattern also takes the control-character spellings of `json.control-escapes`.

differences.title: Maps with integer keys: Go writes the keys in string order, a `BTreeMap` in numeric order
differences.go: jsoniter (`jsonutil.Marshal`) and `encoding/json` sort a map's keys as strings, so `"10"` comes before `"9"`.
differences.rust: A `BTreeMap` with integer keys is written in numeric order, `"9"` before `"10"`.
differences.visible_in: Member order of objects written from maps with integer keys
differences.restore: Serialize such maps through their string keys; not planned.

differences.title: Numbers read into `interface{}`: Go makes every one a float64, a `serde_json::Value` keeps integers exact
differences.go: jsoniter (`jsonutil.Unmarshal`) and `encoding/json` read every number into `interface{}` as a float64: `9007199254740993` comes back as `9007199254740992`, `12345678901234567890` as `12345678901234567000`, and `1.0`, `1e2` and `2.0` are written `1`, `100` and `2`.
differences.rust: A `serde_json::Value` keeps an integer exact up to `u64::MAX` and a float as its f64, which serde_json writes `1.0`, `100.0` and `2.0` (`json.float-format`).
differences.visible_in: Numbers in members Prebid holds as `interface{}` (ext maps, `map[string]interface{}` fields), as bidder request bodies and responses carry them
differences.restore: Read such numbers as f64; not planned (D-DECODE).

differences.title: Invalid UTF-8 in JSON strings: Go decodes it, serde_json rejects the document
differences.go: jsoniter (`jsonutil.Unmarshal` and `UnmarshalValid`) keeps an invalid byte as it came (`a`, 0xFF, `b` stays `61ff62`); only `encoding/json`'s `json.Unmarshal` writes U+FFFD (`61efbfbd62`).
differences.rust: The serde derives reject the document (`invalid unicode code point`).
differences.visible_in: The status of requests whose JSON strings hold bytes that are not UTF-8, and the handling of such bidder responses
differences.restore: Replace invalid sequences with U+FFFD and decode again, which is `encoding/json`'s result (a Rust String cannot hold jsoniter's raw byte); not planned (D-DECODE).

differences.title: JSON keys: Go matches struct fields ignoring case, serde matches exactly
differences.go: jsoniter (`jsonutil.Unmarshal`, `UnmarshalValid`) and `encoding/json` match object keys to struct fields ignoring case, so `"ID"` fills `id`.
differences.rust: serde matches keys exactly; another spelling is an unknown key, ignored, and the field is defaulted or missing. A request whose imps are under `"Imp"` has no imps and gets a 400.
differences.visible_in: Requests and bidder responses whose keys differ in case from the field names: the status, or the values the field would have held
differences.restore: A decode pass that folds keys as jsoniter does; not planned (D-DECODE).

differences.title: Lone UTF-16 surrogate escapes: Go decodes them to U+FFFD, serde_json rejects the document
differences.go: jsoniter (`jsonutil.Unmarshal`, `UnmarshalValid`) and `encoding/json` decode a `\u` escape of a surrogate that forms no pair (a high surrogate before a letter, a low one alone, two high ones) to U+FFFD, once per lone surrogate, and the document decodes.
differences.rust: serde_json rejects the whole document, into the derives and into a `Value` alike.
differences.visible_in: Requests whose strings were cut inside an escaped emoji (Prebid.js sends `JSON.stringify` output, which writes a lone surrogate as `\uD83D`), which Go answers with 200 and serde_json would turn into a 400, and bidder responses with such strings
differences.restore: JSONUTIL's decode entry for outside bytes (request bodies, stored data, bidder responses: every place Go calls `jsonutil.Unmarshal` or `json.Unmarshal` on outside input) rewrites each unpaired `\uD800`-`\uDFFF` escape to `\uFFFD` before serde_json reads the bytes, scanning only when the bytes hold a `\u` escape of that range, with string and escape state tracked (orchestrator ruling 7).

restorations.note: `replace_lone_surrogates` runs on outside bytes in `unmarshal`, `unmarshal_valid`, `merge_clone`, `merge_patch`, `find_element` and the lenient readers: a lone surrogate escape in a value or a key decodes to U+FFFD, as both Go decoders give it.
50,000 seeded strings of plain text, escapes, lone surrogates, pairs and broken escapes give jsoniter's bytes or its failure.

differences.title: A lone surrogate escape inside a `json.RawMessage`: Go passes the bytes on, the port writes the escape of U+FFFD
differences.go: jsoniter keeps a raw member's bytes as they came, a lone surrogate escape such as `\ud800` included, and `jsonutil.Marshal` writes them back compacted.
differences.rust: `replace_lone_surrogates` rewrites the escape to `\uFFFD` before serde_json reads the document (`json.lone-surrogates`), so the raw member is written with it. Go and serde_json read both as U+FFFD; a reader that keeps lone surrogates, such as JavaScript's `JSON.parse`, sees the surrogate in Go's bytes.
differences.visible_in: Raw members (`ext` and the like) of bidder request bodies and responses whose input held a lone surrogate escape
differences.restore: Keep the input's bytes for raw members and rewrite only what serde_json reads; not planned (ruling 7 rewrites the bytes before serde_json sees them).

differences.title: Documents edited in place: Go keeps their member order, an edit through a `serde_json::Value` sorts the members
differences.go: Where Prebid edits JSON bytes in place (sjson's `SetBytes`, jsonparser's `Set`), the document keeps its member order and the new member goes where Go puts it.
differences.rust: The port edits a `serde_json::Value`, which is written with every object's members in key order (`preserve_order` is not used).
differences.visible_in: Member order of the exts and bodies Prebid's Go code edits in place, in bidder request bodies and responses
differences.restore: Edit the bytes in place as sjson and jsonparser do; not planned.

differences.title: Merge patch: evanphx drops the null members of objects inside an array it adds, json-patch keeps them
differences.go: `MergePatch` deletes the null members of objects inside a patch's array where the array is new to the document, replaces a value that is not an object, or is the patch itself: `{"a":[{"b":null}]}` merged into `{}` gives `{"a":[{}]}`; over an object it keeps them.
differences.rust: json-patch writes a patch's arrays as they are (RFC 7386), null members included.
differences.visible_in: Merged stored requests, imps, accounts and exts whose patch holds an array of objects with null members, as raw members (such as an imp's `ext`) carry them into bidder request bodies
differences.note: DECISIONS.md proposed `json.merge-patch-quirks` for this quirk; that id names them all here.

differences.title: Merge patch inputs beyond serde_json's limits: evanphx merges them, the port rejects them
differences.go: `MergePatch` merges a document or patch holding a number beyond float64's range (kept as its bytes) or nested 200 levels deep (`encoding/json` reads 10000 levels).
differences.rust: serde_json rejects a number beyond f64's range and a `Value` nested deeper than 128 levels, so `merge_patch` fails with `Invalid JSON Document` or `Invalid JSON Patch`, and a `json.RawMessage` merge in MergeClone with `invalid json on existing object` or `Invalid JSON Patch`.
differences.visible_in: The status of requests whose stored data, first-party data or exts hold such a number or nesting
differences.note: MergeClone's side is pinned by `crates/jsonutil/tests/merge_clone.rs::raw_merge_limits_fail`.

differences.title: Merge patch output: evanphx writes a value it copies with its members as written, json-patch's result sorts them
differences.go: A value `MergePatch` copies from the document without merging into it keeps its member order and its repeated keys (`{"c":{"b":1,"a":2}}` stays so); what it merges or takes from the patch is written with its keys sorted.
differences.rust: serde_json's `Value` writes every object's members in key order, a repeated key's last value kept.
differences.visible_in: Member order of merged stored requests, imps, accounts and exts

differences.title: Merge patch into a `null` document: evanphx fails with `Invalid JSON Document`, json-patch merges
differences.go: `MergePatch` fails with `ErrBadJSONDoc` (`Invalid JSON Document`) when the document is the JSON `null`, whatever the patch (merge.go:127-129 of json-patch.v5). A stored request or stored imp that is `null` fails the auction with a 400 (endpoints/openrtb2/auction.go:1722, 1755).
differences.rust: json-patch merges an object patch as into `{}` and returns any other patch (RFC 7386), so the auction goes on.
differences.visible_in: The status of auctions whose stored request or stored imp is the JSON `null`
differences.restore: A check in front of the merge that returns Go's errors in Go's order (document syntax, patch syntax, null document, then a null or scalar patch), which Prebid turns into its own errors: glue under Rule B (d) if the user restores it.
differences.default: json-patch's result: the patch merges into a `null` document as RFC 7386 says (crates first).
differences.note: DECISIONS.md makes this entry decision-pending without a decision id of its own; `D-MERGEPATCH` names it until DECISIONS.md records one.

differences.title: Merge patch: Go runs evanphx/json-patch v5.9.0's `MergePatch`, the port json-patch 0.2.7's RFC 7386 merge
differences.go: Prebid merges stored requests and imps, the default request, accounts, first-party data, MergeClone's `json.RawMessage` fields, event URLs, targeting and hook responses with evanphx's `MergePatch` (util/jsonutil/merge.go:165, endpoints/openrtb2/auction.go:1711-1755 and ten other files), which departs from RFC 7386 in three cases and writes each value with the spelling it was read with.
differences.rust: json-patch's `merge` follows RFC 7386 and serde_json writes the result. The values agree on RFC 7386's appendix, on every stored-request, stored-imp, account, first-party data, ext and event merge input of the upstream corpora, and on 50,000 seeded pairs outside the cases the other `json.merge-patch-*` entries name.
differences.visible_in: Merged stored requests, imps, accounts and exts, where one of the other `json.merge-patch-*` entries applies
differences.note: Each departure has its own entry and pin: `json.merge-patch-array-nulls`, `json.merge-patch-null-document`, `json.merge-patch-scalar-patch`, `json.merge-patch-spelling`, `json.merge-patch-member-order` and `json.merge-patch-limits`; `crates/jsonutil/tests/merge_patch.rs::seeded_pairs_match_go` classifies the seeded pairs alike on both sides.

differences.title: Merge patch with a `null`, string, number or boolean patch: evanphx fails with `Invalid JSON Patch`, json-patch returns the patch
differences.go: `MergePatch` fails with `ErrBadJSONPatch` (`Invalid JSON Patch`) for a patch that is `null`, a string, a number or a boolean, unless the document is `null` (merge.go:131-133 and 141-149 of json-patch.v5). A bidder config's `{"ext":"abc"}` for `user`, `site` or `app`, merged by MergeClone into a non-empty ext, fails, and Prebid answers 400 with `invalid first party data ext` (firstpartydata/first_party_data.go:267 and 348-353, exchange/exchange.go:302-310).
differences.rust: json-patch returns the patch (RFC 7386), so the ext becomes the string and the auction goes on.
differences.visible_in: The status of auctions whose `ext.prebid.bidderconfig[].config.ortb2` sets `user.ext`, `site.ext` or `app.ext` to a string, number or boolean over a non-empty ext of the request, and the bidder requests that would carry it
differences.restore: The check in front of the merge that `json.merge-patch-null-document` describes, returning `Invalid JSON Patch` for a null or scalar patch after the document checks, so Prebid answers with its own 400: glue under Rule B (d) if the user restores it.
differences.default: json-patch's result: a null or scalar patch replaces the document as RFC 7386 says (crates first).
differences.note: A null patch never reaches `MergePatch` through MergeClone, which keeps the field on null; `D-MERGEPATCH` stands for the decision DECISIONS.md has not named yet.

differences.title: Merge patch output: evanphx keeps each value's spelling and escapes HTML, serde_json writes the values its own way
differences.go: `MergePatch` writes each value with the bytes it was read with (`1.0`, `1e2`, `1.50`, `-0`, `100000000000000000000000`, `\u00e9`, `\/`, a lone surrogate escape) and re-marshals with `json.Marshal`, so `<`, `>` and `&` in strings become `\u003c`, `\u003e` and `\u0026`.
differences.rust: serde_json writes numbers in their shortest form (`1.0`, `100.0`, `1.5`, `-0.0`, `1e23`), `<`, `>` and `&` as they are, escapes decoded and a lone surrogate as U+FFFD; the values agree.
differences.visible_in: The spelling of numbers and strings in merged stored requests, imps, accounts and exts, in bidder request bodies and responses
differences.note: The harness sees these as the `number_format`, `html_escape` and `unicode_escape` classes, which `json.float-format` and `json.html-escape` take.

differences.title: `-0` read into an integer field: Go reads 0, serde_json rejects the document
differences.go: jsoniter (`jsonutil.Unmarshal`, `UnmarshalValid` and `MergeClone`) and `encoding/json` read `-0` into a signed integer field, a typed one (openrtb2's enums) or a pointer to one as 0, and reject it for an unsigned one; a float64 field holds -0.
differences.rust: serde_json parses `-0` as the float -0.0, which every Rust integer type rejects (`invalid type: floating point`), so the document fails to decode and `merge_clone` fails; an `f64` field holds -0.0, written `-0.0` (`json.float-format`).
differences.visible_in: The status of requests, and the handling of bidder responses, that hold `-0` in an integer member (`w`, `h`, `api`, an enum)
differences.restore: Read `-0` as 0 wherever serde asks for an integer (a deserializer adapter around serde_json's, or typegen's integer helpers); not planned (D-DECODE).

differences.title: Nesting depth: Go reads 10000 levels, a `serde_json::Value` stops at 128
differences.go: jsoniter and `encoding/json` accept 10000 levels of nesting (9999 arrays inside the outer object) and reject a deeper document, whether the deep value lands in a `json.RawMessage`, in an `interface{}` or in a key they skip.
differences.rust: serde_json stops a `Value` at 128 levels, the outer object included (127 arrays inside it fail with `recursion limit exceeded`), and reads a `RawValue` or skips an unknown key at any depth, 10001 levels included.
differences.visible_in: The status of requests whose JSON nests 128 levels or more, and the handling of such bidder responses

differences.title: A nil `json.RawMessage` without `omitempty`: Go writes no value at all, the port writes `null`
differences.go: Prebid's `RawMessageExtension` writes nothing for a nil `json.RawMessage` that `omitempty` does not drop, as a field, a map value, a slice element or on its own, so `jsonutil.Marshal` returns bytes that are not JSON (`{"ext":}`, `[,{"x":1}]`).
differences.rust: serde writes `None` as `null` (`{"ext":null}`), which is JSON; under `omitempty` (`skip_serializing_if`) both drop it.
differences.visible_in: Bodies `jsonutil.Marshal` writes from a type whose `json.RawMessage` field has no `omitempty` and is nil
differences.restore: None that serde allows: a serializer cannot write a member without a value, and the bytes Go writes are not JSON.

differences.title: NaN and infinities: Go fails the write, serde_json writes `null`
differences.go: A NaN or infinite float, and a float32 that overflowed to +Inf, fails the marshal: `jsonutil.Marshal` returns `FailedToMarshal` with jsoniter's `unsupported value: NaN` after the field's path, and `encoding/json` returns `json: unsupported value: NaN`. The auction endpoint then records `/openrtb2/auction Failed to send response` among the analytics errors and sets the request status `RequestStatusNetworkErr`, and the response body is not written (endpoints/openrtb2/auction.go:394-397).
differences.rust: serde_json writes `null` in the value's place before any Formatter sees it, so the document goes out.
differences.visible_in: Response bodies, and the request status metric, when a float in the response is not finite
differences.restore: A `serialize_with` helper on every f32 and f64 field that fails as the Go writer does; not planned (orchestrator rulings 2 and 5).

differences.title: A document that is JSON null: Go leaves the target's zero value, serde_json rejects the document
differences.go: `jsonutil.Unmarshal`, `UnmarshalValid` and `json.Unmarshal` return no error for the document `null`, whitespace around it or not, and leave a struct and a number as they were, a map and a slice nil, and a string empty (jsoniter) or as it was (`encoding/json`), so an adapter that reads a bidder's `null` body into `openrtb2.BidResponse` goes on with an empty response. `MergeClone` leaves the value as it was.
differences.rust: `unmarshal` and `unmarshal_valid` fail with `invalid type: null` for every target but an `Option`, which reads `None`; `merge_clone` leaves the value as it was, as Go does.
differences.visible_in: The bidder errors (`ext.errors`) and metrics of auctions where a bidder answers `null`, and the error Prebid answers a request body of `null` with
differences.restore: Read the document through `null_default`, with a `Default` bound on `unmarshal` and `unmarshal_valid` (no other crate calls them yet): glue under Rule B (a) if the user restores it on evidence that bidders or clients send such documents.
differences.default: serde's result: the document fails to decode (crates first).
differences.note: D-DECODE restores null on a non-pointer field and does not say whether that reaches a whole document. Prebid branches on the failure (a bidder error and its metrics where Go goes on with an empty response), so the entry waits for the user, as `json.merge-patch-null-document` does.

differences.title: null as a slice element or map value that is not a pointer: Go keeps the zero value, serde rejects the document
differences.go: jsoniter (`jsonutil.Unmarshal`, `UnmarshalValid`) and `encoding/json` read null as an element of a slice, or a value of a map, whose type is not a pointer as that type's zero value, as they read it for a field (`json.null-into-value`): `[1,null]` into `[]int` gives `[1,0]`, `["a",null]` into `[]string` gives `["a",""]` and `[null]` into a slice of structs one zero struct. `MergeClone` does the same, and a pointer element is nil.
differences.rust: `null_default` covers fields only, so a `Vec` or `BTreeMap` whose element is not an `Option` rejects the document (`invalid type: null`); an `Option` element reads `None`, Go's nil, and `merge_clone` reads every element as Go does.
differences.visible_in: The status of requests, and the handling of bidder responses, whose arrays or maps hold null where Prebid reads a number, string or object (`bcat`, `api`, `format`, a bid's `adomain`); `JSON.stringify` writes `NaN`, `Infinity` and `undefined` array elements as null
differences.restore: Counterparts of `null_default` for slice and map fields, which read each element as an `Option` and turn `None` into the default, put by typegen (ORTB-SERDE) on every slice and map field whose element is not a pointer: glue under Rule B (a) if the user restores it, on the ground D-DECODE gives for fields (real traffic sends these nulls).
differences.default: serde's result: the document fails to decode (crates first).
differences.note: D-DECODE restores null on a non-pointer field and does not say whether that reaches slice elements and map values. `JSON.stringify` writes `NaN`, `Infinity` and `undefined` array elements as null, as it writes `NaN` and `Infinity` members, so the entry waits for the user.

differences.title: `null` for a value field: Go keeps the zero value, serde rejects the document
differences.go: `null` given to a field that is not a pointer or interface (a number, bool, string, struct, slice or map) leaves the field at its zero value, and the document decodes.
differences.rust: serde rejects the document (`invalid type: null`).
differences.visible_in: Requests and bidder responses that send `null` for a value field
differences.restore: JSONUTIL and ORTB-SERDE: container `#[serde(default)]` plus typegen's `null_default` deserializer on every value field, so a `null` leaves the default; real traffic sends these nulls.

restorations.note: `null_default` with a container `#[serde(default)]` leaves each value field's zero value, as `jsonutil.Unmarshal`, `UnmarshalValid` and `json.Unmarshal` do; ORTB-SERDE's typegen puts it on the generated types.

differences.title: `null` for a `json.RawMessage`: `encoding/json` keeps the bytes `null`, a plain serde `Option` reads nothing
differences.go: `json.Unmarshal` (`encoding/json`, in the 13 production files DECISIONS.md lists: 8 adapters, floors/fetcher.go, gdpr/gvl_vendor_ids.go, pbs/usersync.go, analytics/pubstack/config.go and privacysandbox/topics.go) keeps the four bytes `null` in a `json.RawMessage` given null and writes them back as `null`; jsoniter (`jsonutil.Unmarshal`, `UnmarshalValid`, the auction request among them) leaves the field nil.
differences.rust: A plain `Option<Box<RawValue>>` reads null as `None`, which is jsoniter's nil; `raw_keep_null` keeps `Some(null)`, which `raw_compact` writes back as `null`, as `encoding/json` does.
differences.visible_in: Requests and bodies built from types Go decodes with `encoding/json`, when the input sends `null` for a raw member
differences.restore: `raw_keep_null` on the `json.RawMessage` fields of the types Go decodes with `encoding/json`, and a plain `Option` where jsonutil decodes (D-DECODE's correction), so each site keeps what its Go decoder does; real traffic sends `ext: null`.

restorations.note: Both decoders' rows: `raw_keep_null` against `json.Unmarshal`, a plain `Option` against `jsonutil.Unmarshal` and `UnmarshalValid`.

differences.title: Numbers beyond float64's range that no field reads: jsoniter fails the document, serde_json reads it
differences.go: jsoniter (`jsonutil.Unmarshal`, `UnmarshalValid`) parses a number it skips (in a `json.RawMessage`, an unknown member, the bytes `IntString` reads) when it has an exponent, and fails the document with `invalid number` beyond float64's range (`1e400`, `-1e309`, `1.8e308`); a number that starts with 0 it parses as a float32, and fails with `value out of range` beyond float32's range (`0.5e39`). `encoding/json` reads them all.
differences.rust: serde_json reads such a number into a `RawValue` or skips it, as `encoding/json` does, and `IntString` reads it as `+Inf` or `-Inf`, as gjson spells it.
differences.visible_in: The status of requests, and the handling of bidder responses, whose raw or unknown members hold such a number
differences.restore: Parse every number serde_json skips as jsoniter's skipper does; not planned (D-DECODE).
differences.note: `crates/jsonutil/tests/readers.rs::seeded_int_strings_match_go` classifies the seeded numbers alike on both sides.

differences.title: Parity documents: Go reads and writes them with `encoding/json`, pbs-parity with serde
differences.go: The `parity` packages read the harness documents (envelopes, adapter inputs and outputs, the outbound meta, health, config and bidders dumps, reset results and traces) with `json.Unmarshal` and write them with `json.Marshal` and a `json.Encoder`: a key fills the member it matches ignoring case, the last of repeated members wins, `null` leaves a value member unset, a `null` raw member is kept as `null`, a header pair is padded or cut to two strings, the ID string types take any value, a string that is not UTF-8 reads with U+FFFD, `<`, `>`, `&`, U+2028 and U+2029 are written as escapes, and a NaN that `Session.Record` or `Session.AddAnalytics` gets is a marshal error, noted in the trace in its place.
differences.rust: The documents are serde types that serde_json reads and writes (orchestrator ruling 3), so the JSON entries apply: `json.key-case`, `json.duplicate-keys`, `json.null-into-value`, `json.null-elements`, `json.null-raw`, `json.invalid-utf8`, `json.html-escape`, `json.float-format`, `json.raw-not-compacted`, `json.struct-from-array`, `json.error-texts`, `json.negative-zero-int` and `json.non-finite`. A header pair of another length is refused (`invalid length 1, expected a tuple of size 2`), the stage, status and decision IDs are closed enums that refuse a name outside the registry (`parity: unregistered parity.StageID value "made.up"`), a NaN is recorded as `null` (an analytics object that is NaN makes `analytics[].object` null, which the trace schema refuses), a raw value that is not JSON has no Rust form, so nothing records one or notes it as Go does, and the crate's own messages quote with `{:?}` where Go uses `%q`. Each document compares equal with Go's as a JSON value, which is how the runner compares the two servers' documents.
differences.visible_in: The parity harness's documents, which only the Go runner writes and reads: their spelling, and how a document the runner never writes reads
differences.restore: `encoding/json`'s reading on the documents' derives; not planned (orchestrator rulings 2 and 3).

differences.title: `ParseIntoString` on bytes that are not JSON: gjson reads a value out of them, the port leaves the target unset
differences.go: `jsonutil.ParseIntoString` reads with `gjson.ParseBytes`, which takes a value out of an unterminated string, a number with bytes after it, a plus sign, `nan` and a literal cut short.
differences.rust: `parse_into_string` reads the bytes with serde_json and leaves the target unset when they are not one JSON value.
differences.visible_in: Nothing in production: the one caller reads `regs.ext.gpc`, a value the request's decoder has already read (openrtb_ext/request_wrapper.go:1279-1282)

differences.title: A document that fails to decode: Go leaves what it read in the target, `unmarshal` returns no value
differences.go: jsoniter (`jsonutil.Unmarshal`, `UnmarshalValid` and `MergeClone`) writes each member into the caller's value as it reads it, so after an error the value holds the members read before the failure, a slice element that failed as its zero value, and the whole document when other bytes follow it. Prebid goes on with that value where a hook rejects the auction (the response carries the request's id and analytics log the request: endpoints/openrtb2/auction.go:468, 516), for a bid's native asset types (exchange/bidder.go:475), and in the goldbach and dmx adapters (adapters/goldbach/goldbach.go:52, adapters/dmx/dmx.go:165).
differences.rust: `unmarshal` and `unmarshal_valid` return the error alone, so such a caller goes on with the type's default. `merge_clone` into the default leaves Go's value where a member fails, but drops a slice element that fails and leaves nothing where the document is not JSON or other bytes follow it, since it reads the whole document first.
differences.visible_in: The id of the response to an auction a hook rejected whose body fails to decode and the request analytics log for it, the native asset types of bids whose imp's native request fails to decode, and goldbach and dmx requests built from an ext that fails to decode partway
differences.restore: A decoder that writes into the caller's value member by member as it reads, which serde's derives do not offer (`merge_clone` comes closest); not planned (D-DECODE).

differences.title: A float written with a leading `+`: jsoniter reads it into a float field, serde_json rejects the document
differences.go: jsoniter's float decoders pass a number that starts with neither a digit, a minus nor a dot to `strconv.ParseFloat`, which accepts a leading `+`, so `jsonutil.Unmarshal`, `UnmarshalValid` and `MergeClone` read `+1.5`, `+.5` and `+1e2` into a float64 or float32 field, and `-+1` as -1 (iter_float.go:207-214, :299-337). An integer field, a skipped member and `encoding/json` reject it.
differences.rust: serde_json rejects the document, as `encoding/json` does.
differences.visible_in: The handling of bidder responses, and the status of requests, with such a number in a float member (a bid's `price`, an imp's `bidfloor`)
differences.restore: Accept a leading `+` where serde reads a float; not planned (D-DECODE).

differences.title: `json.RawMessage` on write: Go compacts it, serde_json writes a `RawValue` as it was read
differences.go: `jsonutil.Marshal` writes a `json.RawMessage` through Prebid's `RawMessageExtension` (registered at main.go:23-25), which runs `json.Compact`: whitespace goes, nothing is escaped, and for bytes that are not JSON nothing is written and no error returned, so the output (`{"id":"1","ext":}`) is not JSON. `json.Marshal` and the endpoints' Encoders compact it too, HTML-escaping inside it unless `SetEscapeHTML(false)`, and fail on bytes that are not JSON (`error calling MarshalJSON for type json.RawMessage: unexpected end of JSON input`).
differences.rust: A `RawValue` is written as it was read, whitespace included, and serde_json cannot build one from bytes that are not JSON.
differences.visible_in: Ext members and other raw JSON in bidder request bodies and in responses
differences.restore: JSONUTIL: `raw_compact`, the equivalent of Prebid's own `RawMessageExtension`, which typegen puts on every `json.RawMessage` field. This is Prebid logic, not library glue; the escaping inside stays `json.html-escape`.

restorations.note: `marshal` and `marshal_raw` compact every raw value they write, a map value, a slice element and the value itself, as `jsonutil.Marshal` does wherever it reaches one: `RequestWrapper`'s ext maps, the exchange's sanitized imp ext and the auction endpoint's resolved imps.
50,000 seeded raw values with whitespace between and inside their tokens are written as `jsonutil.Marshal` writes them.

differences.title: `StringInt`: `"+5"` reads 5 where Go fails, and `"-"` fails where Go reads 0
differences.go: `jsonutil.StringInt` parses a string's text with jsonparser's `ParseInt`, which rejects a leading `+` and reads a lone `-` as 0.
differences.rust: `StringInt` parses with `i64::from_str`, which reads `+5` as 5 and rejects `-`; every other input reads alike.
differences.visible_in: Bidder params read as `StringInt` (appnexus `placementId` and `placement_id`, pulsepoint `cp` and `ct`, connectad, nativo, freewheelssp and targetvideo) whose string is `+` and digits, or `-`
differences.restore: Port jsonparser's `ParseInt` grammar; not planned.
differences.note: `crates/jsonutil/tests/readers.rs::seeded_string_ints_match_go` classifies the seeded inputs alike on both sides.

differences.title: A JSON array where a struct is expected: Go rejects it, the serde derives read its elements as the fields
differences.go: jsoniter (`jsonutil.Unmarshal`, `UnmarshalValid`) fails with `expect { or n, but found [` where it reads a struct from an array.
differences.rust: A derived struct reads a JSON array as its fields in declaration order (`["x",5]` fills `id` and `n`), and `[]` as its defaults under `#[serde(default)]`, so the document decodes.
differences.visible_in: The status of requests, and the handling of bidder responses, that send an array where an object is expected
differences.restore: Generated `Deserialize` impls that accept only a map, as Go does; not planned (D-DECODE).

differences.title: A surrogate escape before an escape it does not pair with: Go's decoders disagree, the port reads it as jsoniter does
differences.go: jsoniter (`jsonutil.Unmarshal`) reads the surrogate as U+FFFD and the next escape on its own; `encoding/json` pairs that next escape with the one after it; gjson (`IntString`, `ParseIntoString`) turns the two escapes into one U+FFFD, dropping the character the second spells (`\ud800\u0041` gives U+FFFD alone).
differences.rust: `replace_lone_surrogates` follows jsoniter everywhere: U+FFFD, then the next escape read on its own (`\ud800\u0041` gives U+FFFD and `A`).
differences.visible_in: Strings holding a lone surrogate escape right before another `\u` escape, where Go decodes with `encoding/json` or reads with `IntString` (appnexus `member`) or `ParseIntoString` (`regs.ext.gpc`)
differences.restore: A rewrite per Go decoder; not planned (ruling 7 names one rewrite).

differences.title: A NUL byte after the document: jsoniter ignores it and every byte after it, serde_json rejects the document
differences.go: jsoniter's `nextToken` returns 0 for a NUL byte as at the end of the input, and its `Unmarshal` takes a 0 after the value for the end, so `jsonutil.Unmarshal`, `UnmarshalValid` and `MergeClone` stop at a NUL after the document and ignore what follows it (config.go:345-357, iter.go:181-197). `encoding/json` rejects any byte after the value but whitespace, and a NUL before or inside the value fails everywhere.
differences.rust: serde_json rejects the document (`trailing characters`), as `encoding/json` does.
differences.visible_in: The handling of bidder responses, and the status of requests, whose body ends with a NUL byte (a C string's terminator) or holds bytes after one
differences.restore: End the input at the first NUL byte after the value before serde_json's end check; not planned (D-DECODE).

differences.title: Malformed numbers inside a `json.RawMessage`: jsoniter keeps them, serde_json rejects the document
differences.go: `jsonutil.Unmarshal` and `UnmarshalValid` (jsoniter) keep a number with a leading zero after its minus (`-01`, `[-01]`) in a `json.RawMessage` field as it was written; `encoding/json` rejects it, and every other malformed value fails in all three.
differences.rust: serde_json rejects the document.
differences.visible_in: The status of requests, and the handling of bidder responses, whose raw members (a bid's `ext`) hold such a number
differences.restore: Port jsoniter's skipper for `json.RawMessage` fields; not planned (D-DECODE).

differences.title: Log lines: glog's header with the facade's file and line, against tracing-subscriber's format
differences.go: glog writes `W1118 12:00:00.000000 4242 logger.go:17] message`: the level letter and the date, the time to the microsecond, the PID and the file and line, which through Prebid's logger facade (depth 1, logger/glog.go:37-41) are always the facade's own, `logger.go:17` for a warning.
differences.rust: tracing-subscriber's fmt layer writes `<RFC 3339 time>  WARN <module path>: message`: an RFC 3339 time, the level padded to five characters and the event's target, with no file or line.
differences.visible_in: The server's log output (stderr, as the image runs with `-logtostderr`)
differences.note: The glog calls that bypass the facade (the rules engine's observer.go:14 and :20, and the WURFL module) write their own file and line; no pin covers them.

differences.title: Trace metric deltas: ordered by series keys that quote label values with `{:?}`, not `strconv.Quote`
differences.go: `trace.MetricsDelta` sorts the changed series by `seriesKey`: the metric name and its labels sorted by name, each value quoted with `strconv.Quote` (parity/trace/metrics.go:55-68, 144-163).
